Messages.Author: Orpheus
Messages.Body:
I have been a good Necromancer. I have played the Eternal Jyhad, and
sometimes scored some victories for my side. So, for the coming year (and
the forthcoming expansions), I'd like the following presents :

- new options for the Independents, to make them at least able to compete
with the Camarilla (and therefore the Sabbat)

- a BAN for PTO (no, making another card to kill Inner Circles wouldn't do ;
there are few of them, many non-Camarilla vamps) ; or a verrrrry big errata
(something akin to Golconda : "burn the vampire ; his controller gains his
capacity in pool")

- new options for the G4 Giovanni : if they must exist, let them at least
open different opportunities (more For, PRE and other out-of-clans) instead
of just making them pumped-up copycats of the G2s

- new Necromancy cards. Among other ideas : an action that would give +1
bleed to wraiths (could be burned in D action that costs a pool) ; an action
that transforms a burned mortal ally into a wraith ; a fight card or two
(maneuvers ? something like Flesh of Marble ?).

- new allies or other innovations to give the Giovanni new gaming options.

Provide at least some of these and I'll again do my best to honour you, the
game and its creators by giving offerings in the form of GWs and FGs*.

*Fun Games.

Thank you, Santa Claws.

--
Orpheus

-----------------------
"The World as we know must be destroyed"

FLA

> And I forgot Martial Ritus...

Luck Blow does not give Ventrue Antitribu increased Melee Weapon damage.
It merely allows them (or anyone) to strike with hand or a melee weapon to
inflict +1 damage.

Dapravity does not give Ventrue Antitribu increased Melee Weapon damage.
It merely increases the strength of a vampire by +1, gives him or her +1
stealth when diablerizing and makes him or her unable to recruit allies or
employ retainers.

Martial Ritus does not give Ventrue Antitribu increased Melee Weapon
damage. It merely increases the strength of a Sabbat vampire by +1 for the
duration.

I disagree. As there would still need to be a block made, there could
be a case that the blocking minion can hold the acting minion at bay.

Delaying Until Dawn
Type: Reaction
Requires: Fortitude
[for] If this block is successful, all damage inflicted to all
vampires in the resulting combat is aggravated. The acting vampire may
now choose to cancel this action.
[FOR] As above, but the acting vampire cannot cancel this action as
per Inferior (OK, that's clunky, but I didn't want them unable to
cancel the action by other means like Change of Target).

Delaying Until Dawn Mk II
Type: Reaction
Requires: Fortitude
[for] If this block is successful, all damage inflicted to all
vampires in the resulting combat is aggravated. The acting vampire may
now choose to have this action fail.
[FOR] As above, but the acting vampire cannot choose to have this
action fail.

Morgan Vening

Messages.Author: Luis Duarte
Messages.Body:
De:Orpheus (orphe...@DEADSPAM.free.fr)
Assunto:Dear Santa,
Newsgroups:rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad
Data:2004-12-07 15:23:35 PST

>(...)

>- a BAN for PTO (no, making another card to kill Inner Circles
wouldn't do ;
>there are few of them, many non-Camarilla vamps) ; or a verrrrry big
errata
>(something akin to Golconda : "burn the vampire ; his controller
gains his
>capacity in pool")

>(...)

I'm absolutely against the ban of PTO. This is THE card that makes
people play with Inner Circles. Without PTO you don't have a strong
motivation to invest 11 pool in a single vampire for a vote deck since
you have other common ways to control the table votes.
IMO PTO is already limited:
- You must play an Inner Circle (cap 11) to bypass the capacity
limitation;
- The target must be non-Camarilla (you can burn Beast that is able to
rush you to death but you cannot burn Theo Bell...);
- You must pay 1 blood (minor limitation, i agree with that here);
- It's a rare card hard to trade and expensive to buy.

Besides that, you simply don't play an all-PTO deck, and now without
DU it can be used to burn your predator non-Cam Weenies instead of
keep it for later winning move.

AFAIU if you want to change something in PTO, make it more expensive,
like 3 blood or something. You can play Voter Cap later but you must
have both 3 blood (1 more for Forgotten Labyrinth!) and VC in your
hand.

Instead of trying to ban PTO i'd find more useful other changes.
Here's my wish list to L.Santa J.:
- introduce a capacity limitation in cripts (say an average capacity
of 4 or 5) to control weenie decks without eliminate them;
- modify the First Strike rule so i can find more interesting to build
a Bang Nack Tiger Claws deck...
- i need an event to help me win with my Slaughterhouse deck!
- some change to reduce Dominate/Bleed power approaching it more
closer to Dementation/Bleed efficiency.
- and of course, DON'T BAN PTO!

.- Luis Duarte

Sorry, but superior disciplines out the wazoo, crushing special abilities,

> Without PTO you don't have a strong

It could be used in that role before, and that isn't what makes PTO
overpowered, but you know that...

> AFAIU if you want to change something in PTO, make it more expensive,
> like 3 blood or something. You can play Voter Cap later but you must
> have both 3 blood (1 more for Forgotten Labyrinth!) and VC in your
> hand.
>

Meh. 3 blood on an IC is peanuts. This isn't much of a restriction,
especially considering VC blood replenishment. So you need 4 blood on an IC
for the duration of a referendum... *shrug*

> Instead of trying to ban PTO i'd find more useful other changes.
> Here's my wish list to L.Santa J.:
> - introduce a capacity limitation in cripts (say an average capacity
> of 4 or 5) to control weenie decks without eliminate them;

So I put two 11 caps into a weenie deck (which would probably play Effective
Management, anyways), and never influence them. The problem of weenies
cannot be solved with an average capacity restriction.

> - modify the First Strike rule so i can find more interesting to build
> a Bang Nack Tiger Claws deck...
> - i need an event to help me win with my Slaughterhouse deck!

Just my opinion here (stated before, I know. But no one seems to listen)
Library Mill decks are like bleed decks. If one Mills Responsibly, the
likelihood of success (in the form of Game Wins) increases. The idea of
grinding a player's whole deck away for a win in VTES will never be a tier 1
deck concept. If Milling ever reached a level of competitive efficiency, I
think it would be ultimately bad for the game, since it would mean a single
deck would be capable of milling the decks of two or three other players in
about eight to ten turns of play. Card burn like that would be too obscene.

Remember, we don't obsolete old sets in this game. Once the cards to
build a deck like that are in the game, the concept is there for good.

Regards
DaveZ
Atom Weaver

Messages.Author: Daneel
Messages.Body:
On 14 Dec 2004 02:43:48 -0800, Luis Duarte <luis....@netcabo.pt> wrote:

>> Sorry, but superior disciplines out the wazoo, crushing special
> abilities,
>> +2 bleed, and 4 votes is _plenty_ of reason to play a vampire.
>

> I believe most people won't be convinced to invest 11 pool in a single
> vampire that can bleed for 3 and have 1 more vote than a Justicar...

Okay, I can't help it. "I think 64k ought to be enough for everyone."

> Regarding bleed, bleed decks rely mainly on Action and Act Modif
> cards, and the less capacity the vampire have the better. About Vote
> decks actually the vote control is achieved mainly using cards like
> Awe, Bewitching Oration, Animal Magnetism, Ventrue Headquarters, Fee
> Stakes, etc. Once again the lesser capacity the better which means
> also that the base votes in a vote deck is usually composed by
> Princes, Primogens, Archbishops, Cardinals or Bishops. with 11 pool
> you can influence 2 vampires distributing the risk of loosing one
> vampire and increasing the chances to increase the base titles or
> votes.

This is foolishness. Paying 11 pool for a vampire is a tough commitment,
true. You can get nuked and then its all gone. BUT. Underestimating the
power of +2 bleed and 4 votes is foolhardy indeed. We're talking about
permanent things here.

Controlling Volker and Rake, for example, gives you:
2 minions with: CEL pot and PRE aus cel pot
That's two actions each turn and 8 total levels of disciplines.
If you bleed with both, you do 2 pool damage.
You also have 4 votes.

Controlling Arika gives you:
1 minion with: DOM FOR OBF PRE aus cel
That's one action each turn (-50%) and 10 total levels of disciplines.
(+25%)
If you bleed, you do 3 pool damage. (+50%)
You also have 4 votes. (+0%)

If you consider cards like Freak Drive, Minion Tap, Obedience, Govern
the Unaligned and Voter Captivation, you stop worrying and end start
loving Da Bomb (that's the Lady for ya).

Sheesh, where's a Derek when you need one.

--
Bye,

Daneel

playing any cards. Costing 11 is typically made up with some trivial
combination of Minion Tap, Ancient Influence, Political Stranglehold
and, when appropriate, Voter Captivation.

For instance,
http://www.thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#2k3fomaa
http://www.thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#elsegundo2k1
both devote half their crypt slots to IC members and have no PTO.

Another with half IC's has but one PTO, seemingly because
it can -- that is, the PTO isn't what made Shaun decide to
pack 6 ICs into its crypt:
http://www.thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#octoberrust2k1
(a fate shared by many of the decks that have more than one
IC in the crypt -- splash a single PTO in after the fact
just because you can).

A few others from a brief search of the TWD :
